clue.text: Disease, when linked to top quality outstanding, lives

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
best means of top quality
o/s is the accounting abbreviation for outstanding, as of an unpaid bill
lives means exists, which is 'is'

explanation.surface: A doctor naming an illness that strikes only the finest people while they live.
explanation.definitionFit: A lung illness caused by inhaling mineral fibres once used for insulation, so a kind of disease.

clue.text: Get lighter energy for nothing in English resort

indicators.note: energy for nothing means the letter for energy stands where the zero-shaped letter was

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast
O looks like zero, nothing
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker at a seaside town who sheds pounds while doing nothing energetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow lighter in colour or mood is to become brighter.

clue.text: Guy from Fife turning guy inside out

indicators.note: turning means the letters of the Scottish county name are churned round
inside out here means the inside is removed, leaving only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A man from the Scottish county of Fife turning his fellow inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges FIFE into EFFI; GY is guy with its inside gone. Guy is a straw figure burnt on Bonfire Night in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a stuffed figure of Guy Fawkes burnt in Britain each November, an image of a person.

clue.text: See 20
Western character Daisy's smitten by?

parts.note: Daisy is a traditional name for a dairy animal; someone who strikes such a beast is, read literally, a cattle hand of the Wild West

explanation.surface: Asks which cowboy film hero a woman called Daisy has fallen for.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle herder of the American West, a cowboy, a stock figure of Western films.

clue.text: Support for camera, yet turned up as old clothes washer

parts.note: a dolly is a wheeled platform carrying a film camera

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: yet means but, as in 'small yet strong'

explanation.surface: A camera tripod that has turned up somewhere, oddly, as an old washing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub in which laundry was agitated with a wooden pole, an old washing device.

clue.text: See 20
As the hourglass figure went (and so the modelling career)?

definitions.text: As the hourglass figure went (and so the modelling career)?

parts.words: As the hourglass figure went (and so the modelling career)?
parts.note: a model whose waist thickened lost her shapely figure, taking a fruit-like form, and the phrase also means went badly wrong, as her career did

explanation.surface: A model's slim shape spreads and her career collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means went wrong, and literally describes a body broad at the hips.

clue.text: Put formally, tennis great with appropriate round decoration

parts.note: Steffi Graf, tennis great, written formally with initial and surname is S Graf
fit means appropriate, suitable
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A tennis champion, formally addressed, receives a suitable round decoration, like a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles; 'put formally' gives her initial with the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A technique of scratching through a top layer of plaster or glaze to reveal a contrasting colour, used as ornament.

clue.text: Large island reduced by a gas

parts.note: Australia, a vast island, shortened to its informal name Oz
a means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: A big island shrunk by a gas, like a climate-change story.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule, a gas found in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Hot on the heels of swinging single people

indicators.note: on the heels of means coming right after, so the hot letter goes at the end
swinging means the letters of the word single are swung about

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Hot on the trail of swinging singles: a racy party scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinging' turns SINGLE into ENGLIS, and 'on the heels of' puts H after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation of England taken as a whole, a people.

clue.text: State tennis legend's song and dance

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania, a US state
Rod Laver, Australian tennis great, twice won all four Grand Slams in a year

explanation.surface: A tennis star's tune and routine, as if performing on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A song and dance is a fuss about nothing, which is what this word for tedious bother means.

clue.text: Desirable girls generally try to put out — time for resistance?

indicators.note: put out means the words try to are knocked out of their order
time for resistance means the time letter replaces the resistance letter

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Suggests a man trying to put a date with attractive women out of his mind, needing time to resist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the R in TRY TO for T, giving TTYTO, which 'put out' then rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for attractive women collectively, a crude and now dated usage.

clue.text: Made acceptable, the thing breathes in windy Andes

indicators.note: breathes in means the piece is put inside the windswept mountain name
windy suggests the letters of Andes are blown about

parts.note: it means the thing
something that breathes lives, it is

explanation.surface: A creature cleaned up so it could breathe in the gusty South American mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windy' turns ANDES into SANED, and 'in' puts IT and IS between SAN and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean something up, removing offensive parts, is to render it acceptable.

clue.text: Movement, if impaired with sloe gin, embracing fellow?

indicators.note: embracing means the jumbled letters wrap round the fellow letter
impaired suggests the words are damaged and rearranged, like a drinker's faculties

explanation.surface: A man too drunk on sloe gin to move, a fellow hugging his bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impaired' rearranges IF and SLOE GIN into SIGNOLIFE, and 'embracing' places F inside after SIGNO.
explanation.definitionFit: Any stirring of a body shows it still lives, so movement is an indication of being alive.

clue.text: Sequined, it's designed to be unsettling

definitions.note: a verb sense, to be unsettling, matching the verb meaning to make uneasy

indicators.note: designed means the letters are made into a new pattern

parts.note: only the two letters of it go in; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A sequinned dress deliberately created to disturb onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone uneasy or worried, a rare verb built on the noun for anxiety.

clue.text: Blowing the whistle on football team's once popular number

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing, blowing the whistle on others
The Blues is a nickname for several football clubs, Chelsea for one

explanation.surface: A whistleblower exposes a football club's former hit song.
explanation.walkthrough: The title was a hit in the 1950s for Guy Mitchell and Tommy Steele.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1956 hit record, so a song that was popular in its day.

clue.text: Milliner ran two houses free from error

indicators.note: houses means the words contain the answer within them, spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A hat maker who managed two homes without a single mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to err, infallible, a description of something faultless.

clue.text: Swimming nude over foam, so not allowed alcoholic drink?

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second
swimming means the letters of nude move about

parts.note: to foam is to rage, as an angry person foams at the mouth

explanation.surface: Skinny-dipping teenagers frothing over not being served at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Too young by law to buy or drink alcohol, so barred from the bar.

clue.text: Battle location having small advantage: opportunity to retreat

parts.note: edge means an advantage

indicators.note: to retreat means the word goes backwards

parts.note: room means opportunity, scope, as in room for improvement

explanation.surface: A general sizes up a field with a slight advantage and a chance to fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: Sedgemoor in Somerset saw the last pitched battle on English soil, in 1685.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somerset site where Monmouth's rebels were defeated in 1685, a famous battlefield.

clue.text: The big picture shows balls in the possession of football side

parts.note: balls are formal dances
with means having, as in 'a man with money'
Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers football club

explanation.surface: The overall view: a football club ends up owning the balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1990 Kevin Costner film, so a picture that is big, both long and Oscar-laden.

clue.text: Down with … what did you say about holy man?

parts.note: down means sad, low in spirits

indicators.note: about means the exclamation is turned round

parts.note: uh is a puzzled interjection asking for something to be repeated

explanation.surface: Someone, mishearing, asks again about a holy man feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu ascetic or wandering mendicant, a type of holy man.

clue.text: See 8
Ostentatious flâneur one's seen off on this occasion

definitions.text: one's seen off on this occasion

indicators.note: ostentatious suggests the stroller's letters are flaunted in a showy new arrangement

explanation.surface: A showy idler, a boulevard stroller, who has been sent away on this occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: A flâneur is a man about town who strolls idly.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremony at which a dead person is given a last send-off.

clue.text: Musical note (quarter-second) often posed by web site visitors

definitions.text: often posed by web site visitors

parts.note: fa is the fourth note in sol-fa
Q is the abbreviation for quarter

explanation.surface: A musical note lasting a quarter-second, often posed by web site visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Frequently asked questions are those a site's visitors commonly raise.

clue.text: Vast area ripe for development — look into it

indicators.note: into it means the piece is put inside the rearranged letters
ripe for development suggests the letters are open to being redeveloped into a new order

parts.note: air means look or appearance, as in an air of calm

explanation.surface: An estate agent's pitch: a huge plot ready to build on, check it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for development' turns RIPE into PRIE, and 'into' puts AIR inside after PR.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge, flat grassland of North America, so a vast expanse.

clue.text: See 24
Rock band gets job making important roof timber

parts.note: Queen is the British rock band of Freddie Mercury
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A rock group gets work on a major building project.
explanation.definitionFit: One of two upright supports in a roof truss, a key structural beam.

clue.text: Female, put coarsely, eg "sheila" or "bird"

indicators.note: coarsely put means the letters are crudely rearranged

explanation.surface: Slang words for a woman, such as Australian sheila or British bird, put crudely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put coarsely' turns EG SHEILA into ISHEAGLE. Sheila is Australian and bird British slang for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey that hunts fish, a type of raptor.
